readme: APPEND-ONLY. A name here was removed from the authoring surface and may never return with another meaning.
memqlbreaking refuses a deletion that has no entry here; that refusal is the gate (memql#5389, D21).
It refuses the other direction too: a name here that reappears in the surface is reported, because files in the wild still carry the old spelling and would load under the new meaning without a word.

To un-reserve a name -- when the same thing genuinely comes back -- delete its entry in the SAME change that brings it back, so the un-reservation is a line a reviewer reads rather than an absence nobody sees.

`annotations`, `constructs` and `functions` reserve WORDS, the things that can be handed to something else. A construct's body clause, an annotation's receiver and a shape's projected keys are part of a contract rather than words; a break in one is reported and acknowledged by re-capturing component/language/surface/2026.json in the same change.
The retired @use* FAMILY (@useConcept, @useShape, @useQuery, ...) is a prefix rule in component/language/annotations, not a list of names, so it is reserved by that rule rather than by an entry here.
The concept-field ledger (component/conceptfields/concept-fields.snapshot.json) is the same rule for concept fields, and predates this file.

annotations.async: refused on automations since memql#2712: an automation already runs asynchronously off its event or schedule trigger, and nothing read the annotation.
annotations.audit: removed from the allow-lists in memql#989; nothing read it.
annotations.caller: #221: @caller on a shape became @actor, and the field accessor was renamed with it (caller.X -> actor.X).
annotations.clientExecution: epic memql#4988: it dispatched a tool's body to the connected browser over the client-tool relay, which went with the cognition node. Every tool now needs a server-side @handler.
annotations.concepts: epic #2281: a shape binds its concept in the two-identifier signature, `shape <Concept> <name>`, with the concept imported by a file-top use line.
annotations.deprecated: memql#5375: rendered by help() and editor hover and read by nothing that changes behaviour. Deprecation is said in the construct's @description.
annotations.enabled: memql#5375: constructs are enabled by default, so @enabled was an explicit no-op that read like a switch. @disabled is the one that deactivates.
annotations.idempotent: removed from the mutation allow-list in memql#989; nothing read it.
annotations.immutable: memql#5375: declared metadata with no write guard behind it, so it read as a constraint while constraining nothing. A field that must not change is enforced by the mutation that writes it.
annotations.kind: an action is always one primitive capability call, and a composite of several is an automation, so there was nothing left to mark.
annotations.latestMode: memql#5375: the engine derives time-dependence from `asOf latest` in the body, so the annotation restated it and could contradict it.
annotations.namespace: memql#5375: a concept's namespace is its domain directory, or that directory's one-line namespace.pin (#2614). The annotation could only restate one of those or silently disagree with it.
annotations.nocache: memql#5375: one annotation for the cache TTL, with @cache(0) meaning never.
annotations.permission: buried (#2631 ruling close-out / #2713), the @role twin: documented but never enforced. Access control lives at the actor layer -- RBAC plus the @public per-row-authz classification.
annotations.rateLimit: memql#5375: Tool.RateLimit was cloned and copied into a Function field nothing reads, so the declared ceiling did not exist. The live ceilings are the provider chokepoint in ai_guard.go and the run budget in component/work.
annotations.reliability: reliability is runtime state the engine keeps, not something the source declares.
annotations.retry: removed from the allow-lists in memql#989; nothing read it.
annotations.role: buried (#2631 ruling / #2709); documented but never enforced -- nothing ever checked the value at runtime. Access control lives at the actor layer.
annotations.schedule: D15, epic memql#5370: a scheduled automation is written @trigger(schedule="<cron>"), the one spelling. memqlmigrate --rewrite=bodies rewrites it.
annotations.scopes: memql#5375: Tool.Scopes was advertised on the gRPC tool descriptor and checked nowhere, so it read as an authorization gate while gating nothing. @requiresCapability is the real one.
annotations.shape: epic #2281: a spec binds its shape or concept in the signature, `spec <boundName> <name> = row => <predicate>`, with boundName resolved through the file-top use import.
annotations.timeout: removed from the allow-lists in memql#989; nothing read it.
annotations.unique: memql#5375: declared metadata with no uniqueness check behind it (memql#2960), so it read as a constraint while constraining nothing.
annotations.visibility: removed in the genesis simplification: it chose which node types load a construct, and every binary now loads everything while build tags decide which integrations are active.

constructs.import: epic memql#5356, D17: the file-top `import ( ... )` block loaded on the engine and no loader ever read it. A construct is imported with a file-top `use <domain>.<file>.{ names }` line.
constructs.mutate: D13, epic memql#5370: a mutation is declared with the word a call spells -- `mutation <Concept> <name> { ... }`. memqlmigrate --rewrite=bodies rewrites it.

functions.and: edition 2026: the connective is the operator, `a && b`.
functions.coalesce: edition 2026: `a ?? b`, which is also blank-coalescing.
functions.exists: edition 2026: `x != nil`. exists(x) read a blank string as absent, and so does the comparison -- absent, null, nil and "" are one unset value.
functions.list.contains: edition 2026: membership is the `in` operator, `v in <list>`. The graph traversal keeps the name `contains`, which is why only the collection METHOD is reserved here.
functions.mean: edition 2026: the method, `x.avg()`. mean() was an automation-evaluator operand the tree never used.
functions.now: edition 2026: `now` is a reserved ROOT, not a call. The `now()` call form is gone.
functions.or: edition 2026: the connective is the operator, `a || b`.
